QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_29

question.text: In an SIA engagement, 'materiality' governs which outcomes the SIA focuses assurance procedures on. Which definition is BEST aligned with the workbook?

answer.text: Material issues assessed using quantitative and qualitative factors and their effect on the evaluation of the subject matter
Outcomes whose monetary value exceeds 2% of CSR spend
Outcomes that received media coverage in the reporting year
Outcomes the SE's board voted to include in the AIR

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes materiality as the assessment of issues using both quantitative and qualitative factors and their effect on the evaluation of the subject matter. Impact reporting should include an audit trail of stakeholders, outcomes or indicators included and excluded. The Trap: The 2% CSR rule is a Sec 135 spend threshold, not materiality. Media coverage is not a materiality test. A board vote is governance, not assurance materiality. Note: Document materiality using both quantitative and qualitative factors, and disclose included/excluded stakeholders, outcomes and indicators in the audit trail.
